subject: Attestation dossier onboarding pathway for Orchid Financial RFI
messages:
From: Amaya Patel <amaya.patel@orchidcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orchidcorp.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI follow-up — attestation dossier and handoff timeline

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Our procurement/compliance team has started building the RFI response packet and we need a concise way to represent "audit-ready" proof for your security controls. Specifically: a single manifest (index) that maps each SIG/SOC2/ISO control to a named artifact and the canonical storage location, plus a short description of how to access the artifact during our review window.

Can Redwood provide an "attestation dossier" (index + sample artifacts) and confirm last-mile delivery options (SFTP, secure Drive link with restricted access, or an on-demand artifact portal)? Our target is to lock down the RFI packet by EOD next Friday (2027-07-09).

I can share a template if that helps. Who should I coordinate with on your side for the technical proof transfer and timeline?

Thanks,
Amaya Patel
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
Orchid Financial

--
Attachment: rfi_template_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amaya Patel <amaya.patel@orchidcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up — attestation dossier and handoff timeline

Hi Amaya — good to hear from you and glad the demo was useful.

We can absolutely compile an "attestation dossier" that meets the format you described. Proposed approach:
- Deliver a lightweight CSV index that maps control IDs (SIG/ISO/SOC2) to artifact filenames, short access notes, and proof type (log, config, screenshot, report).
- Include a representative sample bundle (SOC 2 Type II PDF, TLS cert snapshots, KMS key rotation runbook excerpts).
- Provide a temporary, access-controlled Drive folder for initial review plus an SFTP option if you need vault-style transfer.

Kimberly will lead artifact curation and naming conventions. Mina will validate the SOC 2 export and coordinate the cryptographic evidence (KMS rotation logs).

Proposed timeline:
- Today: we intake your template.
- By Tue 2027-07-06: draft dossier and sample artifacts for an initial review.
- By Fri 2027-07-09 EOD: final package delivered and access links provided.

Does that cadence work? If you want to accelerate any items (e.g., an earlier SOC2 extract), let us know and we can prioritize.

Jordan
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Amaya Patel <amaya.patel@orchidcorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up — attestation dossier and handoff timeline

Amaya — adding specifics on how we'll structure the dossier so your review team can parse it programmatically: 

Index format (CSV) columns: control_framework, control_id, control_name, artifact_name, artifact_type, artifact_location, access_instructions, retention_scope, redwood_contact

Artifact naming convention (examples):
- RED_SOC2_2026_T2.pdf (official report)
- RED_KMS_ROTATION_2026-05.log (key rotation audit)
- RED_TLS_CERT_SNAPSHOT_frontend-20270601.txt

Access options:
1) Google Drive folder (recommended) with time-limited viewer + audit logging. We'll supply accounts and a read-only share link.
2) SFTP drop with one-time credentials (for audit teams that require file transfer protocols).
3) Secure artifact portal (we can provision a temporary portal view; access requires a short-lived token).

Security notes: all artifacts containing secrets or PII will be redacted; full raw logs can be made available under an NDA and via direct SFTP with IP allowlisting.

I'll start assembling the index after we get your template. Also attaching our quick-run "KMS access runbook" (excerpts) and the SOC2 extract you can reference for the control mapping.

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments:
- kms-access-runbook.pdf (excerpt)
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (redacted official report)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orchidcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amaya Patel <amaya.patel@orchidcorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up — attestation dossier and handoff timeline

Jordan / Kimberly / Mina — thanks, that level of detail is exactly what we need. A couple of clarifications from the compliance reviewers: 

1) For KMS rotation logs, can you indicate whether the logs show per-rotation key fingerprints (we require proof of rotation per key ID)?
2) For the Drive option, can you add a short explanation in the CSV for the retention policy tied to each artifact (we want to show how long Redwood retains each provenance artifact)?

If you can confirm both items in the draft index, we'll route the package to our internal security committee the same day. The proposed dates look fine — please proceed.

We appreciate the attachments — send the Drive link when ready and we'll kick off the formal review.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Vendor Risk & Compliance
Orchid Financial

--
Attachment: orchid-reviewers-checklist.pdf (internal checklist stub)
